Create a skill when a repeated job needs durable instructions—not merely because a command exists.

## Start with the contract

Write down:

- the trigger: when an agent should load the skill;
- the outcome: what successful work produces;
- the tools and scripts it may use;
- the permission tier and approval points;
- the verification that proves the result;
- the artifact types or handoff it creates.

Keep `SKILL.md` procedural. Put execution in tools or scripts instead of embedding a second runtime inside the guidance file.

## Minimal layout

```text
my-skill/
  SKILL.md
  skill.json
```

A small guidance entrypoint can follow this shape:

```md
# Purpose

Use this skill when ...

## Workflow

1. Inspect ...
2. Call ...
3. Verify ...

## Approval gates

Ask before ...

## Report

Return ...
```

Create metadata that points to that entrypoint and declares only the capabilities the skill actually uses. See [Skill structure](/build/skills/skill-structure/) for the current fields.

## Test before installing

Validate that:

- the entrypoint and load path exist;
- the compact registry can be generated;
- named tools exist in the current tool manifest;
- permission and approval fields match any runtime manifest entry;
- examples run against the current OS;
- the guidance does not contain machine-specific secrets or paths.

Prefer a focused skill over one large manual that activates for unrelated work.
